2. The facts leading to issuing the Rule, in short, inter alia, is that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 142 of 2003 on 17-9-03 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Dinajpur against the defendants-petitioners for a declaration that the decision dated 14-9-03 relating to amendment of the Constitution of Dinajpur District Bar Association is illegal void without Jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from giving effect and confirming of the said amendment and for a mandatory injunction directing the defendants for holding election of the Bar Association on the basis of the original Constitution. On the same day they filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules I and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure for a temporary injunction restraining the defendants from holding a meeting on 17-9-03 to give effect and confirming of the amendments of the Constitution dated 14-9-03 during pendency of the suit and for a temporary ad interim mandatory injunction against them to hold election of the Association for the year 1410 BS on the basis of the original Constitution and as per direction of the High Court Division passed in its judgment and order dated 6-7-03. The plaintiffs in their application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure stated, in short, inter alia, that the plaintiffs, the President and members of the Executive Committee of Dinajpur Bar Association for the year 1409 BS., during their tenure constituted a 16 member Sub-Committee for amendment of the Constitution of the Samity to meet the long standing necessity and demand of the Bar. The Sub-Committee after hard toil and great efforts prepared a draft recommendations of the amendment under the supervision of plaintiff No.1 which was finally approved on 20-4-2003 by the Sub-Committee under his Presidentship and as 2/3rd majority of the members of the Samity was necessary to finally adopt the same as per Constitution, a meeting was called on 8-5-03 but could not be held due to conspiracy of some interested and vested quarters. Thereafter, on the expiry of the period of the Executive Committee, an ad-hoc Committee (consisting of the defendants) was formed illegally at the instance of the said quarter as per provision of Article 109 of the Constitution of the said Samity. One Mustafizur Rahman, an Advocate and two other members of the Samity brought Other Class Suit No. 43 of2003 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dinajpur on 17-5-03 against the present plaintiffs and 10 others for a declaration that the period of the Executive Committee for the year 1409 BS having expired it is a non-existent committee and cannot function as such. They also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules I and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an ad interim injunction restraining them from functioning as such in any way and conducting any meeting of the Samity or utilising its fund including holding of election, etc. and the learned Joint-District Judge accordingly, restrained them by his order dated 25- 5-03 allowing the application. The present plaintiff No. 1 who was the President of the said Executive Committee and defendant No. 1 in said Other Class Suit No. 43/2003 and others being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of temporary injunction/preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 288 of 2003 in the High Court Division in which Civil Rule No, 305(fm)/03 was issued which was disposed of along with the appeal vide its judgment and order dated 6-7-03. In the said judgment and order the High Court Division directed the ad-hoc Committee formed on 14-5-03 to function as ad-hoc Committee and to hold election as per decision of the ad-hoc Committee within 45 days from the date of receipt of the judgment and discharged the Rule and dismissed the appeal accordingly. 

 3. The plaintiffs of present Other Class Suit No. 142/2003 further alleged in their application under 0rder XXXIX, rules I and 2 that the defendants (the ad-hoc Committee) held a meeting on 14-9-03 and amended the Constitution of Dinajpur Bar Association, 1979 adopting the draft recommendations of the said Constitution Amendment Sub-Committee without requisite 2/3rd majority of the members of the Samity and by showing false and forged signatures of the members in Resolution Book and is going to hold election on the basis of the amended Constitution in violation of the judgment and order of the High Court Division passed on 6-7-03. On the said application filed on 17-9-03 the learned Senior Assistant Judge issued a notice upon the defendants to show cause within 3 days as to why a temporary injunction should not be passed restraining them from holding election on the basis of the amended Constitution and refused to issue mandatory injunction as prayed. The defendants-petitioners appeared before the Court on 20-9-2003 in compliance of the notice and prayed for time for filing written objection. The Court allowed the prayer and also passed another order on the application of the plaintiffs filed in the morning directing the defendants to file Notice and Resolution Books which the defendants complied on the same day with an application for safe custody of those books. The plaintiffs filed another application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code in the afternoon at 2-50 PM praying for issuing temporary ad interim mandatory injunction upon the defendant-petitioners, but the Senior Assistant Judge rejected the said petition and also rejected the prayer of the plaintiffs to take notes of the resolution book and allowed the application for safe custody of those books filed by the defendants. Having been aggrieved by the said order dated 20- 9-03 the plaintiff-opposite-parties preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66/03 before the learned District Judge, Dinajpur and again filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for issuing temporary injunction and for temporary ad interim mandatory injunction against the defendant-petitioners. The defendant-respondents appeared in the appeal and filed written objections denying the material averments of the plaintiffs made in the said application and giving a chronological statement of fact. and events with dates of the formation and functions of the ad-hoc Committee including the date of receipt of the information of the judgment of the High Court Division received from the trial Court, facts and events of the Samity with date leading to amendment of Constitution, formation of election commission, declaration of election schedule and of the application filed by plaintiffs to remove the Chief Election Commissioner. The learned Additional District Judge heard the said application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 on transfer and passed the impugned order dated 2-10-03 granting temporary injunction against the defendants- respondents restraining them not to hold election of Dinajpur Zilla Ainjibi Samity for the year 1410 BS on the basis of the amended Constitution till hearing of the Miscellaneous Appeal and also passed a temporary ad interim mandatory injunction directing them to hold election on the basis of the Constitution of the Samity as it was on 6-7-03, the date of passing the judgment and order by the High Court Division. 

 7. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, took me through the application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the plaintiffs, the written objections filed by the defendants, the documents and papers enclosed with the application under section 115(1) of the CPC marked Annexures A-E including the judgment dated 6-7-03 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Rule No. 305(fm)/03 arising out of FMA No. 288 of 2003, counter-affidavit filed by plaintiff-opposite-parties, affidavit-in-reply filed on behalf of the petitioners including several documents annexed thereto and the impugned order. assailing the impugned judgment and order, he submitted that by making specific findings that the amendments are illegal, violative of Articles 109 and 110 of the Constitution, the signatures in the Resolution Book are false and forged, the amendments are not binding and acceptable, etc., the learned Additional District Judge has, in fact, disposed of the suit and the appeal on merit by the impugned order passed in interlocutory matter and has thus erred in law resulting in an error in the decision of the case occasioning failure of justice. He further submitted that the petitioners (ad-hoc Committee) has done nothing except completing the formalities in adopting the recommendations of the Constitution Amendment Sub-Committee admittedly constituted by the plaintiff No.1 himself as convener and the draft recommendations prepared under his supervision were also approved by the Sub-Committee in a meeting held under his Presidentship which the ad-hoc Committee adopted at the request and demand of the members of the Bar Association in a properly called and attended General Meeting of the general members of the Bar held on 14-9-03 with over 2/3rd majority and there was no illegality in holding the meeting or lack of quorum of the meeting adopting the amendments. He added that the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 himself as President of erstwhile Executive Committee of the Samity for the year 1409 BS did everything as aforesaid to bring about amendment of the Constitution of the Samity and also admittedly called a general meeting of the Samity to adopt those amendments in vain but he is now reprobating the same which is unfair and he cannot do so at the same time. 

 8. It is contended by him that the appellate Court below wrongly found that the ad-hoc Committee amended the Constitution in violation of provisions of Articles 109 and 110 of the Constitution of the Samity inasmuch as there is no provision in the whole of the Constitution, 1979 of the Samity including the provision of Article 37 barring the ad-hoc Committee or authorising any particular Committee to amend the Constitution. Mr Alam asserted that the petitioners rightly amended the Constitution adopting the recommendations made long ago by the Sub-Committee and constituted Election Commission which already declared the schedule of election of the Samity to hold election within 45 days as directed by the High Court Division in its judgment dated 6-7-03. He further argued that the amendments of the Constitution having been adopted in a meeting held on 14-9-03, the appellate Court. below has erred in law in passing the temporary ad interim mandatory injunction directing to hold election as per unamended Constitution restoring the situation which was not in existence on the date of passing of the impugned order on 20-9-03. It is also contended by Mr Alam that the ad-hoc Committee did nothing of its own or at its initiative to amend the Constitution but has only performed the formalities to implement the desire of the general members of the Samity and has thus committed no wrong or illegality or violation of any provision of the Constitution of the Samity. It is also argued by him that although the appellate Court below in its impugned order restrained the defendant- respondents (petitioners) to hold election for the year 1410 BS on the basis of the amended Constitution till hearing of the Miscellaneous Appeal, but it has erred in law in directing them by its ad interim mandatory injunction to hold the election of the Samity on the basis of unamended Constitution by which it has, in fact disposed of the appeal on merit and the same is thus liable to be set aside. He also submitted that the appellate Court below has infringed the order of the High Court Division dated 6-7-03 by issuing temporary injunction restraining the defendant-petitioners from holding election as per its decision as directed by the said order. He also argued strongly that the present suit is a private suit instituted by 3 individual learned members of the Bar and not a representative suit representing the Dinajpur Bar Association and nothing has been stated in the plaint or in the application for injunction nor the appellate Court below found in its impugned order as to how the plaintiffs or any member of the Bar has been aggrieved or injured and will suffer irreparable loss and injury if the injunction is not granted. In support of his submission Mr Alam has cited a number of decisions in the cases between the National Bank of India vs Yakub Mia, reported in 7 DLR 606; Abdul Barek Mia vs ABM Serajul Islam, reported in 20 DLR 501; Md Ashid Mia vs Province of East Pakistan, reported in 22 DLR 694; Khondker Monjur Morshed vs Executive Committee (NB), reported in 28 DLR 449; Abdul Jalil vs Abu Bakar Siddique, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42; Bangladesh Muktijoddha Kalyan Trust vs Nurul Hossain, reported in 44 DLR 22; Ministry of Communication vs Md Ferozur Rahman, reported in 45 DLR 762; Abul Hayat Sarker vs MA Reza, reported in 47 DLR 170; Chairman, Bangladesh Oil and Gas vs Md Abul Kashem, reported in 47 DLR 413; Babul Kanti Das vs Abul Hashem, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 6; Anwarul Hakim vs Ramiz Ali, reported in 47 DLR 531; Anwara Begum vs Shamsun Nahar Begum, reported in 49 DLR 364 and Fulbaria Adarsha Market Dokandar Malik Samity vs Fulbaria Adarsha Markel Khatigrastha Dokandar Kalyan Samabaya Samity and others, reported in 53 DLR 220. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr TH Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, submitted in support of the impugned order reading the findings of the appellate Court below that it has rightly passed the impugned order finding a good prima facie and arguable case and he cannot further' improve the case of the plaintiff-opposite-parties. better than the findings of the appellate Court below.  He also contends that the ad-hoc Committee constituted under Article 109 of the Constitution adopted amendments of the Constitution in violation of the provision of Articles 109 and 110 of the Constitution of the Samity and the function of the ad-hoc Committee was to hold election as per original Constitution according to the Order dated 6-7-2003 of the High Court Division and not to amend the Constitution. Mr Fida M Kamal. the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Mr TH Khan for the opposite parties on 17-1-2004 (the date set for judgment), added repeating the findings of the appellate Court below that it has granted the injunction vide his impugned order on finding a strong prima facie arguable case and irreparable loss to be suffered by the plaintiffs if the defendants are not restrained from holding election on the basis of amended Constitution. He further submitted that the ad-hoc Committee took charge and started functioning on and from 9-7-2003 and amended the Constitution without any authority and without 2/3rd majority of the members of the Samity. He also contended that a discretionary interim relief granted by the lower Court subject to final order passed in the suit on consideration of the materials before it should not be interfered under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in its revisional jurisdiction and as such, it would be proper to direct the trial Court to dispose of the main suit expeditiously, etc. In support of his submission, Mr Fida M Kamal has referred the decisions of the cases between Mansur Ahmed vs Kalipada Chattapadhyaya and others, reported in 11 DLR 1032; Abdul Jalil Munshi and another vs Abu Bakar Siddique, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42; Amirul Huq Shameem and others vs AKM Shamsuddin and others, reported in 49 DLR 77; Md Ashid Ali vs Province of East Pakistan and others, reported in 22 DLR 694; Kalur Hat KC Bilateral School vs Sabbir Hossain Chowdhury and others, reported in 52 DLR 102 and The National Bank of India Ltd., Narayanganj vs Yakub Mia, reported in 7 DLR 606. 

 13. The petitioners were informed the details of the judgment by the trial Court on 2-9-2003 after the Court received the judgment on 27-8-2003. The above order of the High Court Division clearly empowered the ad-hoc Committee formed under the provision of Article 109 of the Constitution of the Samity on 14-5-03 to function as ad-hoc Committee and to hold the election as per its decision within 45 days from the date of receipt of this judgment. In the meantime being informed of the above judgment of the High Court Division by Mr Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs of that Other Class Suit No. 43/2003 when the ad-hoc Committee took steps for appointment of Auditor which is a condition precedent to hold election, a learned Senior member who was the Government Pleader opposed the same giving out that no such step should be taken by the ad-hoc Committee before receiving the judgment of the High Court Division as it is evident from Annexure H. It appears from Annexure 1 that in a subsequent meeting one Mr Md Mozharul Islam, a learned Member of the Bar, mentioned that the approved draft amendments of the Constitution has been lying long for adopting the same which should be adopted in a General Meeting and requested the ad-hoc Committee to convene a General Meeting to that effect. Accordingly, the petitioners convened a general meeting- on 14-9-03 and adopted the recommendations of the Sub-Committee duly approved by the Sub-Committee on 20-4-2003 under the President- ship of Mr Khatibuddin Ahmed, President of District Bar Association, Dinajpur, the present plaintiff-opposite party, No. 1 and plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 were the members of that Sub- Committee. The approved proposed amendments of the said Constitution of the Samity has been enclosed with affidavit-in-reply of the petitioners and marked as Annexure-F which shows that the proposed amendments were made under the supervision of the present plaintiff-opposite party No.1 who was President of the Bar at that time and the same was also approved by the Sub-Committee under his Presidentship which has been adopted without any addition or alteration by 2/3rd members of the Bar Association in a General Meeting held on 14-9-03 convened by the petitioners. Thereafter, the petitioners formed an election commission on 17-9- 03 which declared election Schedule vide Annexure-D to hold election on 10-10-2003 within 45 days as directed by the High Court Division. It appears from Annexure D 1 that said Mr Khatibuddin Ahmed, the plaintiff No. 1 and few others including other 2 plaintiffs made an application on 20-9-03 to the defendant petitioner No. 1, the President of the ad-hoc Committee to remove the Chief Election Commissioner and appoint some other Advocate to the said post and still brought the present suit on 17-9-2003. 

 14. The trial Court having refused to grant temporary injunction on an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 filed' by them on the same date and again having refused to Issue ad interim temporary mandatory injunction on 20-9-2003, the plaintiff-opposite-parties filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Dinajpur and again filed aforesaid application for temporary as well as temporary ad interim mandatory injunction under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2. The same was transferred to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge. The learned Additional District Judge by his impugned order allowed the application and granted temporary injunction as well as temporary ad interim mandatory injunction against the defendant- petitioners clearly and specifically finding that the ad-hoc Committee has no power to amend the Constitution under Article 109 of the Constitution of the Samity, that the amendments made by the ad- hoc Committee are illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs as those were made illegally and in violation of the provisions of Articles 109 and 110 of the Constitution. The appellate Court below further found that the amendments were made without quorum being not supported by 213rd members of the Samity as required under Article 110 and that the same has been passed by showing false attendance by forging the signatures of the members of the Bar and, as such, the said amended Constitution should be treated as illegal and not acceptable in law, etc. 

 15. Castigating the above findings, Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, categorically submitted that by giving above findings the appellate Court has granted entire relief to the plaintiffs in interlocutory matter on merit pending hearing of the suit. Neither Mr TH Khan nor Mr Fida M Kamal, the learned Advocates for the petitioners, could controvert the same. On the other hand, Mr Khan submitted that he cannot make out a better prima facie case for the plaintiffs than found by the appellate Court below as quoted above. The above findings of the appellate Court definitely touches the merit of the case and amounts to a judgment on merit pending disposal of the suit. The appellate Court has virtually left nothing to decide in suit on merit. The impugned order shows that it has made specific findings that the amendments were adopted without quorum of 213rd majority, that the signatures of the members of the Bar as shown in the Resolution Book are false and forged, etc. The appellate Court below gave its above findings on disputed and controversial issues involved in the suit pending hearing, on the affidavits filed by some members of the Samity and without taking any evidence which is thus, not sustainable in law. Those findings also tantamount to disposal of the suit on merit in interlocutory matter. Mr Fida M Kamal has submitted that a discretionary order in terms of temporary injunction granted subject to final order passed in the suit should not be interfered in revisional jurisdiction. But the impugned order shows that the appellate Court below has left nothing but passed a final order in discretionary manner. The decision he referred in support of his above submissions, as reported in 11 DLR 103 in the case between Mansur Ahmed vs Kalipada Chattopadhyaya and others, I have no reason to disagree with the principle enunciated in the said case. But the learned Counsel has missed the sentence at para 8 of the decision that" No Court should go into the merit of the suit in which temporary injunction is prayed for", and at paragraph 9 that "It is a discretionary power of the Court to grant or not to grant injunction. If the Court exercises its judicial discretion, the High Court is not to interfere under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure." Mr Kamal has missed words that "No Court shall go into the merit of the suit" and the words that "if the Court exercises its judicial discretion". In the instant case the appellate Court below has passed the impugned order on merit of the case which does not come within the principle of a 'judicial discretion'. Hence this decision is not of any help to him. The other decisions referred by him are also of no help in the facts of the case. 

 16. Mr Khan as well as Mr Kamal, the learned Advocates for the petitioners, have also failed to show that the present suit is a representative suit filed on behalf of the members of the Dinajpur District Bar Association nor they have been able to show as to how the plaintiffs or any other members of the said Bar Association have been aggrieved or injured by the amendment of the Constitution adopting the recommendations already made and approved by a Sub-Committee under the supervision and presidentship of plaintiff No. 1. There is also nothing either in the plaint or in the application for injunction as to how the plaintiffs or for that matter any member of the Bar shall suffer irreparable loss if the injunction was not granted nor there is any finding in the impugned order that the balance of convenience was in favour of the plaintiffs making them entitled to get an order of injunction in any form 

 17. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 has admitted in his application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 that the recommendations for amendment of the Constitution was made by a Sub-Committee constituted by the executive committee of which he was President and those were also approved by the Sub-Committee under his Presidentship and he took the initiative unsuccessfully to adopt those amendments. It also appears from Annexure D1 that all the three plaintiffs are the signatories in that letter in which they requested the President of the ad-hoc Committee to remove the Chief Election Commissioner. From all these facts, apparently admitted and prima facie true from the Annexures which has not been controverted by the opposite parties, that the plaintiffs were very much a party to entire initiative and process of amendment of the Constitution and also took the initiative to adopt the same. It is thus the decision of the plaintiffs which has only been implemented by the petitioners as a matter of formalities without any addition or alteration. The plaintiffs thus being a party to the same should not be allowed to blow hot and cold at the same time as per settled principle held in the case between Nur Banu vs Nur Mohammad and others, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 182, where it has been held that a party should not be allowed to approbate and reprobate at the same time. The conduct of the plaintiffs-opposite-parties appears unfair and mala fide. They also failed to show, even prima facie, that they have been prejudiced injured or in any way aggrieved by the amendment of the Constitution. Order of injunction, in whatever form, is an equitable relief and in order to invoke the same, an aggrieved plaintiff must come bona fide with clean hands with a prima facie case of h is loss and injury showing that if an injunction is not granted he/they will be prejudiced and suffer irreparable loss and injury or his right will be throttled. An order of mandatory injunction or mandatory ad interim injunction is an extremely harsh and highly discretionary order passed at the discretion of the Court to restore a situation existing on the date of filing of the suit or occurred after filing of the suit arid in breach of any order of the Court. Such order cannot be passed to restore or bring back a situation which was not in existence on the date of filing of the suit or of passing of such an order on fulfilling the above conditions. But in the instant case none of the above conditions was existing at the time of filing of the suit or of passing the impugned order.
